title: Where Unblock Stands

short.lead: Another session built the Overview screen and the note importer on Wednesday, and you merged both. My blockers work from Tuesday is still on its own branch, unmerged, and its code is the first design you rejected. Before I build the steps design, I want to tidy that up.
short.hint: Tap a card for the detail behind it.
items: Overview screen (pull request #15): the week ahead and a card for each life area; you called it "works well". Note importer (pull request #20): Keep, text, Markdown and Word exports go into a notes library on your phone, in a Notes tab on the Sort screen. The importer merged at 08:58 UTC and the deploy after it succeeded.
Nothing. I ran main's full test suite here: 221 pass, 0 fail.

Pull request #9, "Blockers: name what is in the way, and deal it instead", still holds the rejected design, where each blocker becomes its own task. The steps design you approved exists only as model pages and decision entries on that branch. It is 33 commits behind main. A test merge shows the code merges cleanly; only two doc files clash.
Your answer to the first choice below, on what to do with the blockers pull request (#9).

Main's state notes are wrong in four places. Blockers is listed as "0%, not started", because the other session never saw my branch. Focus Deck's data is marked as not re-checked live, though you checked it on your S26 on the 13th. The importer is called "not yet merged", yet its pull request (#20) is merged. Finally, the "archived in Keep" badge is said never to show, but the code now shows it (app/js/notes-view.js, line 52).
Nothing from you; I fix these on the new branch.

Eight issues are finished in code and merged, but still open. Each feature has four: Overview (#10 to #13) and the importer (#16 to #19). For both, the issues cover building the logic, adding the screen, a real-browser check, and the write-up.
You close them once you've tested; I never close issues myself.

changes: Closed without merging; its branch stays on GitHub.
Closed; the design pages and decisions are copied to the new branch
Closing keeps every commit, so nothing is lost and it can be reopened. Only the code is dropped: the steps design replaces it.
A fresh branch from today's main for the steps work.
It already holds this page. The model pages and the three decision entries from the blockers branch get copied onto it, and main's out-of-date notes get fixed.
The design work sits on a branch 33 commits behind main.
One branch level with main that holds the design and the corrected notes.
The next pull request you test is built on what's actually live.
A page of small issues, each one named and counted, for you to approve before any code.
Same format as the Overview and importer build plans: what each issue builds, how it's checked, and what you test at the end.
choices: What should happen to the blockers pull request (#9)?
Its code is the rejected design; the commits stay on GitHub.
Nothing changes until you decide later.
Merging it would put the rejected blockers-as-tasks design on your live app.
What should I do after that?
The design you approved on Tuesday, as small issues for you to approve.
Tell me what in your reply, for example the triage build plan.
The steps design is approved but has no build plan yet; triage has none either.

wrapup.summary: A catch-up on what changed since Tuesday, and a clean-up before the steps work starts.
wrapup.changing: Nothing yet. With your OK: the blockers pull request (#9) closes, the design work is copied to a fresh branch, and main's out-of-date notes get fixed.
wrapup.blocking: Your answers to the two choices.
wrapup.next: I write the steps build plan as a page for you to approve.
